gap: None of the results ChatGPT got works out Ah per day in a northern winter for each kit, or the cost of each Ah/day. At 1.9 peak sun hours the VEVOR 20W makes about 2.08 Ah/day at $16.80 per Ah/day, and the SUNER 20W Ultra makes the same at $33.60. Every 10 W kit makes about 1.04 Ah/day, which falls short of the 1.2 Ah/day lost to a 50 mA parked-car drain.
standout_why: I compared against energyforthetaking.com (rank 3 in ChatGPT's results) and solarbatteryscout.com (rank 5 and rank 13), which ChatGPT got but did not cite, and gopowersolar.com (rank 13 in chat 2). energyforthetaking gives a 20–50 mA parked-car drain and about 1.2–1.4 A for a generic 20 W panel, but no prices and no Ah/day figure. solarbatteryscout gives only wattages, a generic 'typical 10-watt solar maintainer can provide 0.5 amps' and no prices. GoPower gives generic 10 W and 20 W Ah/day by region using its formula W × PSH × 0.7 ÷ 12.8 V, but it covers only its own kits, has no 12 W row, no prices for any named maintainer and no comparison against car drain. No result ties a named product's price to the Ah/day it delivers, and none flags that a 10 W kit misses a 50 mA drain in a northern winter. ChatGPT's own card showed the SUNER 20W Ultra at $85.95, but the maker's store lists it at $69.99 today. $85.95 is the price of the different BC-20W Pro.
decides: For a car parked through a northern winter, buy a 20 W kit rather than a 10–12 W one. 10 W yields about 1.04 Ah/day against up to 1.2 Ah/day of drain, 12 W about 1.25 Ah/day, which barely covers it, and 20 W about 2.08 Ah/day, which covers it 1.7 times. Among the 20 W kits, the VEVOR 20W at $34.90 costs half as much per Ah/day as the SUNER 20W Ultra at $69.99. The SUNER 20W Ultra beats SUNER's own 12W Ultra on value ($33.60 vs $48.00 per Ah/day), so ChatGPT's $59.95 12 W pick is the weaker buy. The OptiMate Solar DUO 20W costs $81.70 per Ah/day and is listed as unavailable.
